heading: AASDD CLI
summary: A command-line tool for verifying, scaffolding, exporting, importing, diffing, and graphing AASDD specs.
invariants: The tool never overwrites or modifies any existing file.
All output is written to stdout; all errors and diagnostics are written to stderr.
Exit code is `0` when the ability completes without error, non-zero otherwise.

abilities.heading: Diff
abilities.purpose: Compares two spec directories and reports all structural differences between them.

rows.Description: The first spec directory (baseline).
rows.Name: `left`

rows.Description: The second spec directory (compared against left).
rows.Name: `right`

rows.Description: All structural differences found.
rows.Name: `result`

invariants: Both `left` and `right` are parsed into their structured representations before comparison.
`result.changed` is `true` if and only if `result.entries` is non-empty.
Every entry in `result.entries` references a path that exists in at least one of the two specs.
Comparison is structural, not textual — whitespace and formatting differences that do not change parsed content are ignored.

rows.Condition: `left.path` does not exist.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `left.path` is a file, not a directory.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `right.path` does not exist.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `right.path` is a file, not a directory.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: A file under either directory cannot be read.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

abilities.notes: `--verbose` enriches each entry with the full detail of what changed within the construct. Without it, only the path, kind, and construct type are shown.

abilities.heading: Export
abilities.purpose: Serializes a spec directory into a portable structured file that can be stored, transferred, or used to reconstruct the original directory.

rows.Description: Path to a spec directory to export.
rows.Name: `source`

rows.Description: Destination file path for the exported output. Omit to write to the output channel.
rows.Name: `output`

rows.Description: Summary of the export operation.
rows.Name: `result`

abilities.outputs_note: The data written to `output` (or the output channel) is a serialized [SpecExport](../../concepts/representation/concept.md#specexport) — a structured, semantic representation of the spec directory. The serialization format is determined by the implementation — see `decisions/` for the rationale.
invariants: `source` must be a directory.
Every spec file (`spec.md`, `ability.md`, `concept.md`, `scenario.md`, `decision.md`) under `source` is represented in the export. All other files and hidden entries are excluded.
Abilities, scenarios, sub-abilities, concepts, and decisions are each parsed into their respective structured types.
`result.output_path` is empty when output is written to the output channel.

rows.Condition: `source` does not exist.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `source` exists but is not a directory.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: An output file cannot be written.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

abilities.notes: The `--verbose` and `--progress` flags inherited from the root command have no effect on `export`.

abilities.heading: Graph
abilities.purpose: Generates a dependency graph of a spec directory showing how abilities, concepts, decisions, and scenarios relate to each other.

rows.Description: The spec directory to graph.
rows.Name: `target`

rows.Description: The output format. Defaults to `Mermaid`.
rows.Name: `format`

rows.Description: The rendered graph.
rows.Name: `result`

invariants: Every ability, concept, decision, and scenario in the spec directory is represented as a node.
Sub-abilities are connected to their parent ability with a `sub-ability` edge.
When an ability's inputs or outputs reference a concept type, the ability is connected to that concept with an `input` or `output` edge.
When a scenario's trace references an ability, the scenario is connected to that ability with a `traces` edge.
`result.content` is valid source in the requested format — parseable by Mermaid or Graphviz respectively.
`result.node_count` equals the number of distinct nodes in the graph.
`result.edge_count` equals the number of distinct edges in the graph.

rows.Condition: `target.path` does not exist.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `target.path` is a file, not a directory.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: A file under `target` cannot be read.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

abilities.notes: The graph is written to stdout. `--verbose` has no effect. `--progress` has no effect.

abilities.heading: Import
abilities.purpose: Reconstructs a spec directory on disk from a previously exported snapshot.

rows.Description: Path to an exported snapshot file to import.
rows.Name: `source`

rows.Description: Path to the directory to reconstruct. Must be empty or nonexistent.
rows.Name: `output`

rows.Description: Summary of the import operation.
rows.Name: `result`

invariants: `output` must be an empty directory or a nonexistent path.
Every parsed record in the export produces a Markdown file on disk at `output/<record.path>`.

A round-trip (`export` followed immediately by `import` into an empty directory) produces a directory that is structurally equivalent to the original: all spec files are present at the same relative paths, and the semantic content is identical.
`result.file_count` equals the number of files written to disk.

rows.Condition: `source` does not exist.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `source` exists but is not a file.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `output` exists and is non-empty, or exists as a non-directory.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: `source` cannot be decoded as a valid snapshot.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

rows.Condition: A file cannot be written to the output directory.
rows.Effect: Error written to stderr; exit code non-zero.

abilities.notes: The `--verbose` and `--progress` flags inherited from the root command have no effect on `import`.

sub_abilities.heading: CollectViolations
sub_abilities.purpose: Applies a rule set to a spec directory and returns all violations found.

rows.Description: The spec directory to evaluate.
rows.Name: `target`

rows.Description: The rules to evaluate against the directory.
rows.Name: `rule_set`

rows.Description: When `true`, `ok  <relpath>` is written to the error channel for each validated item: `.` after directory-level rules, and the file's path relative to `target` after each file matched by at least one file-level rule.
rows.Name: `progress`

rows.Description: All violations found, or an empty list if the directory is fully conformant.
rows.Name: `result`

sub_abilities.outputs_note: `result.spec_file_names` is the deduplicated, sorted list of basenames that at least one file-level rule in `rule_set` applies to.
invariants: For every rule in `rule_set.rules`, every file under `target` whose filename matches `rule.applies_to` is evaluated against that rule.
Every violation in `result.violations` has a `rule` value that matches the `id` of a rule in `rule_set.rules`.
Every violation in `result.violations` has a `severity` copied from the corresponding rule.
Every violation in `result.violations` has a `description` copied from the corresponding rule.
Every violation in `result.violations` references an existing path under `target`.
`result.passed` is `true` if and only if `result.violations` contains no `Error`-severity violations.
`result.aasdd_version` equals `rule_set.aasdd_version`.
`result.rule_count` equals the number of rules in `rule_set.rules`.
`result.spec_file_names` contains exactly the set of `applies_to` values from file-level rules (rules where `applies_to` ≠ `"directory"`), deduplicated and sorted.
When `progress` is `true`, exactly one `ok  .` line is written after directory-level rules, and exactly one `ok  <relpath>` line is written per file matched by at least one file-level rule.

rows.Condition: `target.path` does not exist.
rows.Effect: Error propagated to caller.

rows.Condition: `target.path` exists but is a file, not a directory.
rows.Effect: Error propagated to caller.

rows.Condition: A file under `target` cannot be read due to a filesystem permission or I/O error during traversal.
rows.Effect: Error propagated to caller; partial results discarded.

decisions.heading: InvocationChannel
decisions.context: All root-level abilities (`Verify`, `Scaffold`, `Export`, `Import`, `ListVersions`, `Diff`, `Graph`) accept inputs that must arrive from outside the tool, which requires choosing how callers invoke the tool and pass arguments.
decisions.requirement: A mechanism for a caller to invoke the tool, supply a target path, and receive output.
decisions.decision:
CLI — the tool is invoked as `aasdd <command> <path> [flags]`. The target path is a positional argument. Results are written to stdout in human-readable form; errors and diagnostics are written to stderr. Exit code signals success or failure.

`Diff` takes two positional arguments (`aasdd diff <left> <right>`) instead of one.

`Graph` accepts an optional `--format` / `-f` flag (`mermaid` or `dot`). Defaults to `mermaid`.

The AASDD version is not supplied as a flag. For `verify`, it is read from the `**AASDD:**` label in `spec.md` (falling back to the latest version if absent). For `scaffold`, the latest version is always used unless `--aasdd-version` / `-v` overrides it.

Two optional diagnostic flags are available:

- `--progress` / `-p`: streams `ok  <path>` to stderr for each validated path as work happens — the root directory after directory-level rules, and each file matched by at least one file-level rule.
- `--verbose`: always prints `AASDD: <version> (<N> rules)` to stderr, and enriches each violation line with the rule's human-readable description.
- `--aasdd-version` / `-a` (scaffold only): the AASDD version to scaffold for (e.g. `--aasdd-version v1`). Defaults to the latest version known to the tool.

`--version` / `-V` is available on the root command only. It prints the tool version derived from the Go module build info (e.g. `v0.1.0`), or `(devel)` for local untagged builds.
